sections.title: Sounds of th
paragraphs: The letters th make three different sounds in English. Its main sound is heard in the word (think) /θɪŋk/, which means to have an opinion or idea. A second sound uses your vocal cords. A rare third sound works like a regular t.

sections.title: How to say th
paragraphs: Put the tip of your tongue gently between your front teeth. Blow air through the small gap without your voice. Now add your voice so your throat shakes. For the last sound, tap your tongue tip firmly behind your upper front teeth. Touch your throat to feel when your voice turns on.

sections.title: Spelling rules for th
paragraphs: The letters th usually make a voiceless sound in content words like (thing) /θɪŋ/, or at the end like (bath) /bɑːθ/. The sound is voiced in small grammar words like (this) /ðɪs/, and between vowels in (father) /fɑː.ðə/. In a few loanwords and names, the letters sound like t, as in (thyme) /taɪm/.

sections.title: Common mistakes with th
paragraphs: Do not replace the sound with s or f. Keep your tongue between your teeth so you do not say sink instead of (think) /θɪŋk/. Do not swap the voiced sound for z or d. Hold the air steady without tapping your tongue against the roof of your mouth.
